problem:
4x - ky = 9
6x + 15y = 2
In the given system of equations, k is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of k?

bad.why: Setting the coefficient ratios 4/6 = -k/15 is a memorized rule plus cross-multiplication, and matching coefficients alone cannot tell no solution from infinitely many.
Eliminating x and requiring the y-coefficient to vanish while the constant does not is a multi-step argument most students cannot set up.
Needs both lines rearranged into y = form before the slope fit, and a slope match alone does not rule out the two lines being the same line.
Typed into Desmos, the same computation still needs the memorized coefficient-ratio rule, which alone cannot tell no solution from infinitely many; the graphs show it.

algebraFirst.description: Sets the coefficient ratios 4/6 = -k/15 (or rewrites both lines in slope-intercept form) and cross-multiplies to k = -10, often without checking that the constants keep the lines apart.

explanationNotes: Explain 'no solution' as 'the two lines never meet', which happens when they are parallel (same steepness) but not the same line. At k = -10 Desmos shows two separate parallel lines; contrast that with two equations drawing one line, which would mean infinitely many solutions.
